name: Optional elements (empty rules)
description: Determiners and adjectives are optional here, written with ε (the empty string). The parser handles empty rules with the Aycock and Horspool technique: when it predicts a symbol that can be empty, it also moves past it straight away.
grammar:
# An educational fragment of English, not a grammar of the language.
S    -> NP VP
NP   -> Det AdjP N
Det  -> "the" | "a" | ε
AdjP -> Adj AdjP | ε
Adj  -> "big" | "old" | "red"
N    -> "dog" | "dogs" | "cat"
VP   -> V NP | V
V    -> "chased" | "sleep" | "sleeps"

examples.text: the big old dog chased a cat

examples.note: Accepted with an empty determiner and an empty adjective phrase.

examples.text: big red dogs chased the cat

examples.note: Rejected. Only one determiner is allowed.
